title: Garden Birds — 2026-07-28
style: A broad fresco-like landscape field with shallow incised plaster geometry: arcade, lunette, garden wall seams, orchard-trunk verticals and restrained seed-tray horizontals. Forms are simplified into elegant silhouettes and fresco-blocked colour masses, with sinopia underdrawing occasionally visible at the edges. Bird markings remain clear but reduced: caps, wing bars, cheek patches, red mask, collar and tail shapes are described with mineral economy rather than naturalistic detail.
palette: Lime white, warm plaster cream, sandstone beige, yellow ochre, pale umber, terre verte, softened brick red, lime-safe ultramarine, blue-grey, muted lemon yellow, iron oxide red, dove grey, bone black, with faint sea-glass green and cool North Sea blue undertones worked into the shadows.
mood: Calm, sun-warmed, civic, intimate, lightly formal, with a quiet northern freshness beneath the summer ochres.

creative_brief.style_guidance: Develop Lime Orchard Fresco as a refined contemporary wall-cycle: a landscape-format fresco panel that feels discovered rather than illustrated, with shallow architectural divisions, softened summer lime light and carefully placed avian citizens. The work should preserve the calm authority of Renaissance fresco while stripping it back to spare modern geometry, mineral colour and breathing negative space. The birds are not decorative additions; they are the civic presence of the wall, each occupying a distinct register within the orchard architecture.
creative_brief.curator_notes: Today’s exhibition should feel like a fragment of a humane public mural from an imagined northern garden court: sun-warmed, salt-softened, orderly but tender. The five species form a quiet society. House Sparrow and Eurasian Tree Sparrow are treated as close neighbours in umber and brick, grounded near plaster cracks and seed-like marks. Eurasian Blue Tit brings the first crisp chromatic note, placed with precision against a muted lemon-branch curve. European Goldfinch becomes the red-faced herald crossing the central architectural rhythm. Eurasian Collared Dove is a pale, suspended figure in the upper lunette, almost a shade cast by summer light. The coastal North Shields atmosphere should enter only through cool undertones, weathered mineral surfaces and an open sense of air, never through literal harbour imagery.
creative_brief.mood: Calm, sun-warmed, civic, intimate, lightly formal, with a quiet northern freshness beneath the summer ochres.

creative_brief.composition: A wide horizontal fresco wall divided into three shallow arcade bays and a pale upper lunette. The lower band carries small cracks, masonry ledges and seed-like marks where the two sparrows gather at slightly different distances. The middle band holds a curved lemon branch supporting the Blue Tit and opening the central rhythm. The Goldfinch crosses the central arch in a poised diagonal, giving the whole wall a gentle pulse. The Collared Dove rests high in the lunette as a pale balancing form. The structure should feel stable, airy and architectural, with generous unpainted plaster breathing between figures.
creative_brief.bird_integration: Represent every observed bird clearly within the fresco language. House Sparrow: low left, compact and warm brown, with recognisable bib, crown and streaked back reduced to umber fresco marks. Eurasian Tree Sparrow: low right or slightly nearer the central crack, distinguished by chestnut cap, white cheek and dark cheek spot, echoing the House Sparrow but more graphic and precise. Eurasian Blue Tit: mid-height on the lemon branch, immediately identifiable at normal viewing distance through blue cap, yellow breast and dark eye stripe, rendered as the sharpest cool-warm accent. European Goldfinch: central crossing figure, recognisable by red face, black-and-white head and yellow wing flash, stylised as a heraldic fresco motif rather than a wildlife portrait. Eurasian Collared Dove: high in the pale lunette, soft grey-beige with a clean dark neck collar and long calm silhouette, integrated as a shade-like architectural presence. All birds should be visibly birds, with simplified fresco contours, mineral colour and restrained secco detailing.
creative_brief.materials: Wet lime plaster ground, marble dust intonaco, sinopia underdrawing, terre verte wash, yellow ochre, lime-safe ultramarine, iron oxide red, pale umber, bone black, casein secco retouching, rubbed pumice abrasion, shallow incised plaster lines, softened dry-brush dusting and minute embedded summer grit for a salt-worn mineral surface.
creative_brief.visual_focus: The viewer should first be drawn to the luminous central arch of warm lime plaster, where incised geometry, rubbed mineral texture and a cool undertone of sea-glass blue create a quiet glow across the wall.
avoid: making the architecture more important than the birds
hiding or abstracting the birds beyond recognition
